findings.label: Periumbilical erythema
findings.evidence: Significant periumbilical erythema and inflammation consistent with omphalitis on admission.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of neonatal abdomen showing inflamed umbilical stump with clamp and surrounding periumbilical erythema/cellulitis. Caption explicitly states omphalitis and in-text confirms inflamed umbilical stump with surrounding cellulitis in febrile infant, matching omphalitis periumbilical erythema.
panels.attribution_text: Fakih et al. A Case of Severe Neonatal Neutropenia Secondary to Late-Onset Sepsis From E. coli Omphalitis.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.101601. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Significant periumbilical erythema and inflammation consistent with omphalitis on admission.
in_text_mentions: On admission, the infant was febrile, irritable, and plethoric. Vital signs were stable. Physical examination was significant for the findings shown in Figure 1: an inflamed umbilical stump with surrounding cellulitis. The anterior fontanelle was soft and flat. Cardiorespiratory, abdominal, and neurological examinations were otherwise normal.
